directAnswer: To enable file extensions in Windows, you need to access the File Explorer options and modify the settings to show file name extensions.
summary: This guide provides steps to enable file extensions in Windows, allowing you to see the full names of files including their extensions.

sections.heading: Understanding File Extensions
sections.body: File extensions indicate the file type and determine which programs can open them. Common extensions include .txt, .jpg, and .exe.

sections.heading: Steps to Enable File Extensions
sections.body: Follow these steps to view file extensions in Windows.

steps.title: Open File Explorer
steps.detail: Click on the File Explorer icon in the taskbar or press Windows + E.

steps.title: Access Folder Options
steps.detail: In Windows 10/11, click on the 'View' tab at the top, then select 'Options' on the right side. In earlier versions, find 'Folder Options' in the Tools menu.

steps.title: Modify View Settings
steps.detail: In the Folder Options window, go to the 'View' tab and uncheck the box labeled 'Hide extensions for known file types'.

steps.title: Apply Changes
steps.detail: Click 'Apply', then 'OK' to save your changes. File extensions will now be visible in File Explorer.

faqs.question: Will this change affect all users on my computer?
faqs.answer: No, this setting is user-specific. Each user account can enable or disable file extensions independently.

faqs.question: How do I revert back to hiding file extensions?
faqs.answer: Follow the same steps and check the 'Hide extensions for known file types' box in the Folder Options.

faqs.question: Are there any security implications to showing file extensions?
faqs.answer: Yes, showing file extensions can help you identify potentially harmful files, but be cautious as some malware may disguise themselves with misleading extensions.

caveats: The steps may vary slightly depending on your version of Windows.
